topics.topic: Declare the UTC time source, microsecond representation and normalization rule, and its backend path to generated backup code
questions: Which concrete UTC wall-clock source supplies this reading, and through which declared time-source backend does it reach the backup code?
When the underlying clock supplies finer-than-microsecond time, how is it converted to the required microsecond value before it is recorded or used as the cutoff?
The passage must become a declared `time_source_policy` delivered to the backup code through IR `system_clock_backend`, including the decided microsecond conversion rule.

Which clock authority supplies this UTC instant, and if its native reading has finer than microsecond precision, is the value rounded, truncated, or obtained from a source that already returns exact microseconds?

The microsecond clock and representation policy must become a declared `time_source_policy` delivered through IR `system_clock_backend`, including the exact normalization semantics the generated code uses.

What exact representation supplies a microsecond clock reading and stores the record instant, and what happens when the underlying wall clock has finer precision: must the time source already return an exact microsecond value, or is the value rounded or truncated before use?

The passage must place the microsecond precision and representation on one declared path to generated code—through the applicable model type, an imported data-provider constant, or the time-source backend—and name that path instead of leaving the value only in prose.

judgement.why: P5 already judged the same unchanged questions about the UTC clock source, precision, representation, and delivery for durable Registry instants.

precedent.topic: Clock source, precision, representation, and reuse for durable Registry instants
quotes: Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10 minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock, which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a suspension; instants Registry records and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
precedent.why: The clock-authority passage is unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the reopening changes did not make its authority, representation or sampling questions matter.

topics.topic: Decide validity and handling of backup records whose instants are not encoded at microsecond precision
questions: What must a release do with an otherwise valid kept backup made under the previous rule, which allowed its record instant to have the full precision that release held rather than necessarily microsecond precision?
Is a readable record whose instant is encoded at a precision other than microseconds valid, or must such a record be treated as unreadable and deleted?

quotes:
The clock is
   read to the microsecond, and a backup's record holds its instant in UTC
   to the microsecond (L16), so the cutoff and every record's instant have
   one precision and are compared as they are, neither rounded nor
   truncated; a backup whose instant is earlier than the cutoff is deleted.

a kept file's record is valid
   when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be
   read, and only a valid one counts as a kept backup
judgement.why: Both passages governing backup-record precision and validity are unchanged in the closed and current A18 texts, and no change since closure made their treatment of other precisions matter.

topics.topic: Decide whether the A18 change requires a new A21 review result
questions: After the current change to A18, must the categories that reference A18 be reviewed again and a new performed-review result be recorded, or is the existing 2026-11-11 review intended to cover this later change?

quotes: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
judgement.why: A18 and A21 are unchanged since State 2 was closed, so there is no current A18 change to reopen the review under this unchanged rule.

topics.topic: Define the reference instant used to construct backup-record instants in required test 7
questions: Relative to which instant must the two backup-record instants be constructed: the retention step's cutoff instant, the instant at which each backup was originally renamed to its kept name, or another instant?
